title: Ann Arbor resident faces felony charge for allegedly billing Medicaid for medical products never delivered
text:
Ann Arbor resident faces felony charge for allegedly billing Medicaid for medical products never delivered
A. T. Archer
An Ann Arbor, Michigan resident faces up to four years in prison and a $50,000 fine after being charged with one felony count of Medicaid fraud for allegedly billing Medicaid for medical products that were never delivered, as part of the DOJ's National Health Care Fraud Takedown efforts.
According to a State of Michigan Felony Complaint Summary, Kurt Robert Hammond of Ann Arbor was charged with Medicaid fraud — False Claim under the Social Welfare Act. The alleged conduct occurred between Jan. 11, 2023, and May 16, 2024, in Ingham County. The charge stems from billing Medicaid for medical products, including female condoms, that were reported as provided to a beneficiary through McLaren Health Plan but allegedly were never delivered. The case is being prosecuted by the Michigan Department of Attorney General's Medicaid Fraud Control Unit.
Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel announced June 23 that Hammond and three other Michigan residents were charged as part of the DOJ's National Health Care Fraud Takedown. Prosecutors allege Hammond, a Lansing pharmacist, billed for large quantities of female condoms the pharmacy never received. Nessel said the Health Care Fraud Division "works every single day to protect the hard-earned money of Michiganders from Medicaid fraud," adding "these four cases are no exception" and the office will "continue to protect taxpayer dollars and this vital program," according to CBS Detroit.
A recent national poll for the Insurance Watchdog Coalition found that 81 percent of likely voters are more likely to support candidates who prioritize cracking down on health care waste, fraud, and abuse.
The DOJ's 2026 National Health Care Fraud Takedown has resulted in charges against 455 defendants involving $6.5 billion in false claims. In 2025, the DOJ charged 324 defendants involving $14.6 billion in alleged false billings, up from 193 defendants and $2.75 billion in 2024, according to the DOJ.
Six metro Detroit residents were charged in 2024 in schemes involving over $2 million in fraudulent billing, $3.4 million in false Medicare claims, and $2.2 million in illegal kickbacks, according to ClickOnDetroit. In 2025, at least 13 Michigan residents were implicated in fraud cases, including one doctor whose false claims resulted in $1.5 million in improper payments and a pharmacy case resulting in a $1.5 million settlement, according to CBS Detroit.
